checks.quoted: **V2 (`extra_buffer`)**: Enables overlap scheduling and branching point caching with `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --page-size 64`.

checks.claim: FLA_CHUNK_SIZE=64 and the mamba state checkpoint interval (--mamba-track-interval, recipes use 64) are the same 64-token grid, explaining cached = 64*floor((L-1)/64)
checks.quoted: --mamba-track-interval The interval (in tokens) to track the mamba state during decode. Only used when --mamba-radix-cache-strategy is extra_buffer. Must be divisible by page_size if set, and must be >= speculative_num_draft_tokens when using speculative decoding. 256 Type: int
checks.note: FLA_CHUNK_SIZE=64 reproduces (Qwen3.5.mdx:134 '`--page-size` must satisfy `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE % page_size == 0` ... (`FLA_CHUNK_SIZE` is currently 64)'). The track-interval default is 256 and only Qwen3.8-Flash-Next sets it to 64: '`--mamba-track-interval 64`: the default of 256 tokens satisfies the constraints ... at the cost of coarser prefix-cache reuse of the recurrent state.' Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 never set it. Two independent knobs, not one grid.

But the page's evidence base is dense/MLA: 'we tested the DeepSeek-R1-671B model under PD-disaggregated deployment' (Ant, 84% TTFT cut) and Novita's Qwen3-Coder-480B (-56% TTFT, 40%->80% hit rate). checks.claim: Speculation on sequential hybrids has acceptance alpha=0.038 vs 0.68 for parallel hybrids (arXiv:2605.01106), so MTP/NEXTN is not a lever
checks.quoted: Parallel hybrids achieve acceptance rates of alpha = 0.68 at draft length k=2 under greedy decoding, while sequential hybrids yield only alpha = 0.038 -- an 18x gap attributable to how each architecture integrates its components.
checks.note: Numbers reproduce verbatim. The mechanism is 'component-aware self-speculative decoding ... isolating the SSM/linear-attention subgraph as a zero-cost internal draft' - a drafterless scheme, NOT MTP/NEXTN. Same abstract: 'For sequential hybrids, generic LayerSkip achieves 12x higher acceptance rates than the component-aware strategy' (approx 0.46). ADJUDICATION: the negative transfer applies to component-aware self-speculation only, so R-CROSS's 'buys almost nothing on our model family' is over-generalised and R-SGL's 'gate MTP on the checkpoint actually shipping MTP weights' is what the evidence supports. Interacts with V-RES-3: vLLM's shared-prefix checkpoint REQUIRES MTP, so 'MTP is not a lever' and 'use --enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint' cannot both be adopted as written.
